findings.evidence: packages/app-backend/src/recovery.ts:77-82 serializes and successfully exports archive metadata without a bound; import at line94 rejects the entire envelope above32MiB. contracts.ts permits100000 files and200-character names, so valid same-version source data can produce a successful archive that this importer cannot restore.
findings.refutation: The metadata cap appropriately bounds offline parsing, and target file-count/byte quotas are checked separately. Those checks do not constrain metadata text to32MiB: even zero-byte files have hundreds of bytes of metadata apiece. No export-side compatible-bound validation exists to prevent reporting an unrestorable archive as successful.
findings.suggestion: Use one shared envelope limit on both paths and reject incompatible export before reporting success, or introduce a compatible bounded streaming format.

findings.evidence: packages/app-backend/src/state.ts:33 structuredClone copies the accepted GenericOAuthConfig[] directly. The installed node_modules/better-auth/dist/plugins/generic-oauth/types.d.mts explicitly supports function-valued getUserInfo/mapProfileToUser/getToken callbacks; structuredClone rejects functions with DataCloneError before runtime creation.
findings.refutation: Data-only fixture providers work, and snapshotting mutable provider input is desirable. However the public options type promises GenericOAuthConfig, not a data-only subset, and these trusted callbacks are ordinary provider configuration supported by the selected library. No validation narrows the contract or explains the rejection.
findings.suggestion: Snapshot mutable configuration while preserving trusted callback references, or explicitly narrow and validate the supported public configuration contract.

findings.evidence: packages/sdk/src/files.ts:25-26 replays initiation using only name/contentType/size/optionalsha and immediately returns a committed result. If sha256 is omitted, reusing the key with different same-length input.data returns the previous bytes silently.
findings.refutation: The lower-level initiation contract binds metadata, not bytes, so this may be an intentional initiation-only retry contract. The higher-level upload signature includes data, however, making the distinction worth documenting or enforcing. This item is informational and does not block.
findings.suggestion: Define the convenience-upload replay contract explicitly and bind/validate content identity when callers expect changed-data collisions to fail.

resolved_findings.resolution: Downloads now have capacity reservation, finite lifetime, request cancellation, revocation polling and shutdown closers. The newly observed setup-size/stat failure leak was also corrected in current source before this report.

PostgreSQL retains a dedicated advisory-lock connection and health fence; local PGlite and filesystem roots have instance locks; runtimeActive denies duplicate runtimes over the same store; filesystem cell markers include immutable store UUID.
Enforced single-runtime ownership removes the already-open second-runtime bypass. Recovery hold is durably written before import bytes/metadata and reloaded on reopen.
writeAll/readAll loop short I/O; append compares a retained partial prefix and resumes the exact chunk before full sync/hash verification and metadata settlement.
files.upload now returns an already committed initiation replay directly instead of completing it again; basic lost-completion-ack replay source issue is resolved.

Owner metadata and applicationLifecycleGuard independently check raw environment deadlines, and the guard now obtains project/environment/configuration/epoch under the existing serialized control transaction.

not_reviewed: This remains an intermediate source pass during active changes, not frozen release approval. File hashes identify report-time materialized source.
Template and final owner UI review are deferred until freeze. Executable test outcomes and actual rendered mobile/desktop layout are not certified here.
No active pentest, external targets, secret reads, dependency scanning or production/test edits were performed. Read-only security-auditor adaptation only.
Advisory/file locks are source-reviewed concurrency enforcement, not native multiprocess or deployed containment qualification.

Recovery archive schema is asserted by TypeScript after authenticated JSON parsing rather than runtime-validated. This pass found no independently reachable public forgery path and makes no hostile signed-archive claim.
The transient instance.guard can remain after a process dies during lock acquisition; this pass does not certify interrupted-startup lock recovery or its operator runbook.
Recovered source configuration is retained as evidence under a durable hold, with no activation route. Full platform/off-host recovery and external-effect reconciliation remain unqualified.

passed_observations: Recovery export preserves local identity/password-hash state while excluding sessions and OAuth access/refresh/ID values from account records.
Import requires a separate environment of the same project, explicit unavailable lifecycle, empty target and matching source HMAC; storage/count/object quotas are checked before copying.
The durable import hold is committed before physical copies; later transaction/copy failure cannot silently reactivate the destination. Failed copies remain in the isolated held target.
The application SDK uses scoped/versioned headers, bounded successful/error JSON parsing, runtime response schemas and explicit AbortSignals, without an owner client dependency.

SSE parsing handles fragmented UTF-8/CRLF and bounded frames; consumer iteration controls cursor advancement, reconnect requests use the last observed cursor and refetch/revoked messages terminate the stream.
Custom routes require application sessions, strict input/output validation and scoped mutation receipts; fixed route paths cannot select control-plane routes.
